newsitem.title: USA: Trans World Airlines sets hiring freeze.
newsitem.headline: Trans World Airlines sets hiring freeze.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc. put a hiring freeze into effect, the airline announced Monday, but said the plan would not affect pilots or other "front-line" employees.
The airline said the job freeze affected administrative and back office areas of the airline. It did not provide other details.
Under an existing pilot hiring plan, TWA will continue to add about 32 pilots a month until late spring, when hiring will slow to about 16 to 24 pilots a month, the pilots' union said.
TWA recently furloughed flight attendants and trimmed other workers as part of its plan to restructure its operations at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York.
St. Louis-based TWA has recently come under attack by some employees.

The International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers voted "no confidence" in the current interim chief executive, Gerald Gitner. The union also threatened court action if TWA's board continued to shrink the airline.
TWA stock rose 6.25 cents to $6.06 in afternoon trading on the American Stock Exchange.
